faqs.q: What does wildlife removal cost in Alexandria?
faqs.a: It depends on the animal, how it got in, and how much sealing and cleanup the job needs. Our crew inspects first, shows you the entry points we found in Alexandria, and gives you a quote after inspection before any removal or sealing work begins — no prices promised over the phone.

faqs.q: Can you get a raccoon family out of a Alexandria chimney?
faqs.a: Yes — spring raccoon mothers in Alexandria often pick an uncapped chimney or a soffit corner to raise young. Virginia prohibits trap-and-relocate, so our crew works under a Commercial Nuisance Animal Permit: the family is removed or evicted at the structure, any release happens on the property itself, and we finish by fitting a proper chimney cap and sealing the entry so the next raccoon cannot use it.

Alexandria.wildlife_intro:
Alexandria's dense row houses and garden apartments sit between the Potomac and wooded stream valleys in Alexandria. Our crew's calls here follow the ground: potomac River shore, Old Town's colonial blocks, Cameron Run and Holmes Run valleys. Raccoons and gray squirrels take attics and chimneys, striped skunks and opossums work yards and crawlspaces, and bats settle older rooflines in summer.

In spring we remove denning raccoon and squirrel families before the young are mobile. Summer brings skunk, groundhog, and snake calls and the bat maternity season, when exclusion waits under Virginia permit conditions. Fall is sealing season in Alexandria — squirrels, rats, and bats all test the same gaps looking for winter shelter, and our crew closes them after the animals are out, because sealing alone rarely holds.
